title: Rectangular block
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. For the first face, draw a loop consisting of four lines. Begin the first line at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and extend it to (0.1579, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.1579, 0.0) and ends at (0.1579, 0.2369). The third line runs from (0.1579, 0.2369) to (0.0, 0.2369), and the fourth line completes the loop by connecting (0.0, 0.2369) back to the origin. Next, draw the second face using another loop of four lines. The first line starts at (0.671, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line extends from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.2369). The third line goes from (0.75, 0.2369) to (0.671, 0.2369), and the fourth line closes the loop by connecting (0.671, 0.2369) back to (0.671, 0.0). Apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire two-dimensional sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions using the Euler angles and translation vector defined earlier. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0592 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction of the normal. The final dimensions of the rectangular block are a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.2369 units, and a height of 0.0592 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the larger block
larger_block = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(0.1579, 0)
    .lineTo(0.1579, 0.2369)
    .lineTo(0, 0.2369)
    .close()
    .extrude(0.0592)
)

# Define the smaller block
smaller_block = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(0.671, 0)
    .lineTo(0.75, 0)
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.2369)
    .lineTo(0.671, 0.2369)
    .close()
    .extrude(0.0592)
)

# Combine the blocks
r = larger_block.union(smaller_block)

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the first face
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1565, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1565, 0.2369) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.2369) \
     .close()

# Define the second face
r = r.moveTo(0.6712, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.2369) \
     .lineTo(0.6712, 0.2369) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0592)

# Block 1: wider slab on the left
block1 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(0.157, 0.2369, 0.0592, centered=(True, True, False))
    .translate((0.059 + 0.157 / 2, 0.2369 / 2, 0))
)

# Block 2: narrower bar on the right
block2 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(0.083, 0.2369, 0.0592, centered=(True, True, False))
    .translate((0.667 + 0.083 / 2, 0.2369 / 2, 0))
)

# Combine into a single compound part
r = block1.union(block2)

import cadquery as cq

# Two separate rectangular blocks sharing the same height (Z) and depth (Y)

# Larger block on the left
block1 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(0.25, 0.2369, 0.0592)
    .translate((0.125, 0.2369 / 2, 0.0592 / 2))
)

# Narrower block on the right, same Y depth and Z height
block2 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(0.06, 0.2369, 0.0592)
    .translate((0.75 - 0.03, 0.2369 / 2, 0.0592 / 2))
)

# Combine the two disjoint bodies into one result
r = block1.union(block2)
